content.title: The Pitt Season 3: Cast, Release Date, and Latest News
content.text: Warrick PageWhat do we know about The Pitt season 3? Read on to find out. Warning: minor spoilers from season 2 ahead.Before season 2 of The Pitt even made it to air, HBO officially renewed the Emmy-winning medical procedural for a third season. Yep, The Pitt season 3 is officially confirmed! HBO CEO Casey Bloys revealed the good news during the Los Angeles premiere of season 2 on January 7.Since its debut in January 2025, The Pitt has been both a commercial and a critical success for the streamer. By mid-season last year, the show was averaging more than 10 million viewers, making it one of HBO Max’s most successful shows ever.In addition to winning the Emmy for outstanding drama series last September, season 1 of the The Pitt received two Golden Globe Awards in 2026: Noah Wyle won best male actor in a television series (drama), and the show won best television series (drama). Based on the glowing reviews rolling in for season 2, we assume that these wins are just the beginning.Here’s what we know about upcoming third season of The Pitt.TVKatherine LaNasa Explains Why Dana Seems So Different in *The Pitt* Season 2“She’s really hypervigilant…”Who is returning for The Pitt season 3?HBO has not confirmed many cast details yet. However, because many of the cast members from season 1 returned for season 2, we assume they’ll also return for season 3—especially Dr. Robbie (Wyle), despite his declining mental health and concerning behavior throughout season 2…Other OG members of the day shift we’re hoping will stick around include charge nurse Dana Evans (Katherine LaNasa), Dr. Langdon (Patrick Ball), Dr. Santos (Isa Briones), Dr. King (Taylor Dearden), Dr. Whitaker (Gerran Howell), Dr. McKay (Fiona Dourif), Dr. Javadi (Shabana Azeez), Princess (Kristin Villanueva), and Perlah (Amielynn Abellera).TV*The Pitt’s* Patrick Ball and Isa Briones Discuss Langdon and Santos’s Long-Awaited ConfrontationIn an exclusive joint interview with *Glamour*, the costars unpack episode 11, *The Pitt* memes, and what’s next for Langdon and Santos.Who isn’t returning?Sadly, we have learned Supriya Ganesh will not return to play senior resident Dr. Samira Mohan in season 3. This makes sense given that Dr. Mohan has been staring down the end of her residency throughout season 2, with none of her superiors suggesting she should continue in the ER. That doesn’t mean we’re not sad about it!No news yet on nurse Jesse Van Horn (Ned Brower), who was arrested by ICE agents during season 2.INT. TRAUMA 1 SC. 39Warrick PageWhat about the night shift?In some good news, Ayesha Harris has been upgraded to series regular for season 3. Harris has played senior night shift resident Dr. Parker Ellis in both seasons 1 and 2. Frankly, I could use an entire night shift spin-off if we get to see more of Dr. Jack Abbott (Shawn Hatosy) and Dr. John Shen (Ken Kirby).INT. TRAUMA ONE SC. 4Warrick PageAnd the season 2 newbies?Season 2 also gave us some newbies we’d love to see more from, including new nurse Emma Nolan (Laëtitia Hollard), med student Joy Kwon (Irene Choi), and Dr. Baran Al-Hashimi (Sepideh Moafi). We could honestly take or leave med student James Ogilvie (Lucas Iverson), but the actor seems like a nice guy!What will season 3 be about?Each episode of seasons 1 and 2 follows the doctors and nurses at a Pittsburgh hospital through an hour of their emergency room shift. The 15-episode seasons take viewers through a single day in real time. We can assume season 3 will follow this format.One thing we do know—season 3 will “probably not” take place during a holiday, according to Wyle. (Season 2 takes place on July 4.) During an interview with Variety at the season 2 premiere, he also guessed that the time jump between seasons will be shorter. “Ten months was a long jump,” he said. “I don’t think we need to make that long of a jump next time.”TVHow Taylor Dearden Became *The Pitt*’s ‘Sweetheart’*The Pitt* star shares her thoughts on Dr. Mel’s neurodivergence and sexuality, as well as her own aspirations for the future as an actor on the rise.Who is joining the cast for season 3?We’re not sure yet! We’ll update this information when we know more.When will season 3 premiere?While we don’t have an exact date yet, we can expect a similar timeline to season 2’s, which premiered roughly a year after season 1. Bloys noted that a procedural show like The Pitt means turnaround time can be a lot quicker and more consistent than, say, a new season of House of the Dragon.“The annual return is really, really important,” Bloys said in November 2025, per Deadline. “I think as an industry, we’ve gotten away from that, and my hope is for something like The Pitt, we aired it in January [2025], it’s coming back in January [2026]. That kind of habitual viewing, not only week to week, but on an annual basis, is really important in terms of setting habits. I was thrilled not only that it worked; that it won the Emmy on top of that was just cherry on top.”This post will be updated.Originally Appeared on Glamour
